note: Round 5 scores annual volatility 10%, maximum drawdown 10%, CVaR(95%) 10% and failure rate 70% -- three risk measures and no return term at all. That inverts round 3's incentive, where annual return carried 20% against volatility's 10%; here there is no return axis to trade against, so lower risk is unconditionally better and every parameter was re-derived rather than inherited. (1) THE RISK MODEL IS HALF SEMI-VARIANCE. Full-sample variance is only one of the three scored risks; drawdown and CVaR are left-tail quantities and a variance-minimising book need not minimise either. Blending the covariance with a semi-covariance of below-mean deviations targets that tail in closed form without changing the solver, its projection or its duality-gap certificate. At the shipped penalty on sp500 the blend takes maximum drawdown from 42.47% to 37.10%, annual volatility from 14.887% to 14.819% and CVaR(95%) from 2.1276% to 2.1123% -- all three scored risks improve -- while the L1 distance to the prohibited SCM minimum variance book RISES from 0.282 to 0.364. It is the only change in five rounds that improved every scored quantity and the compliance margin at the same time. On ftse100 it is mixed rather than uniformly positive (it buys drawdown at a small cost in volatility), which is recorded rather than smoothed over. (2) THE PENALTY IS SET BY A PER-FOLD FLOOR, NOT BY THE SCORE. The anchor term is the only thing keeping the book off the prohibited SCM minimum variance book, and under a pure-risk score every increment of it is pure cost, so the score alone pushes the penalty toward zero -- exactly the direction that reproduces the prohibited book. Measured per fold against the SCM minimum variance book rebuilt from the same training window (reports/round5_compliance_floor.json): at anchor_penalty 0.10 the 5-asset panel has 7 of 100 folds with L1 distance 0.000, i.e. the submitted weights ARE the prohibited book on those folds, and the median distance (0.584) hides it completely. At 0.25 no fold is below 0.10 but the worst is 0.173; at 0.50 the worst fold is 0.240 (sp500), 0.487 (ftse100) and 0.353 (factors). Shipping 0.50 costs 0.070 of simulated rank score against 0.05 and 0.013 against 0.25. It is taken because the binding dataset is sp500, where the worst fold is 0.240 at every penalty from 0.25 upward -- raising the penalty to 1.0 improves ftse100 and factors but changes sp500 by 0.003, so the extra compliance buys nothing on the constraint that actually binds and costs 0.010 of score. 0.50 is therefore the point where the floor is met with 2.4x to 4.9x headroom at the smallest score sacrifice available. (3) WHAT WAS NOT DONE. Shorting is not used: the brief sets shortselling = FALSE and budget = 1.0, and both are asserted per fold. The prohibited books are avoided structurally, not asserted -- no code path forms 1/n, none forms 1/sigma, and the covariance is Ledoit-Wolf shrunk and Marchenko-Pastur denoised with an anchor term in the objective. (4) A CALIBRATION WARNING ABOUT THE METRIC ITSELF. The L1-to-SCM-GMVP distance is a diagnostic, not a test. Measured over eleven legitimate reference methods on the same folds (reports/round5_margin_calibration.json), NCO reaches 0.000 on sp500 and factors and 0.006 on ftse100, and MinVariance(Denoise) reaches 0.000 on factors -- while EqualWeighted and InverseVolatility, which are prohibited BY NAME, sit at L1 1.1-1.5. A small distance on one fold therefore does not by itself indicate a violation; what the floor above rules out is a systematic regime in which the anchor has stopped acting, which is a property of the construction path rather than of any single fold.
